title: Prove no D-exponent-0 owner index clears the x1 block
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Scoped proof. No new κ. The selected conditional value stays `781451/250000000` from the selected record (PR #6030). This does not change the selected frontier.

On the published two-edge feed, every owner-indexed D-exponent-0 left map of the four final banks that keeps `x0 = D1 Q^{-1}` has x1 coefficient

```text
(const - m0 C1) D1 + (1 - m0 x) Q^{-1} C3 D1 D3
```

with `x = Q^2 (I + Q) C1 Q` and `const = Q^{-1}(C1 Q C1 - I)`. The second summand is never zero. The Q-letter parity character sends `I + Q` to 0 and `Q^{-1} C1` to `-1`, so `m0 x = 1` is impossible. Keeping y0 zero fixes `m1 = const - m0 C1` and does not cancel the summand. Banks 0, 1, and 2 have zero y1, and `m3 = 0`, so y1 stays zero. The four stored banks are only read.

Evidence class: a proof in the predecessor's formal algebra. The multiplier space is infinite. This is not a word census, not a bounded search, and not a theorem that the monomial vanishes in every physical quotient.

The unique index that also clears the D1 line is `m0 = const C1`, `m1 = 0`, `m2 = Q^{-1} C1 Q^2 C1 Q`. Its fresh image keeps x0, y0, and y1 as required and leaves the single monomial `Q^{-1} C1 Q^2 C1 C3 D1 D3`. That image removes the three published keys and is still not the autonomous row `[A, 0, 0, 0]`.

## Task and overlap

Base: `17469fff78c22941280f04d39dc5a1faee09c840`. Task: `joint-query-controller`, scope refined. This answers the x1-column question left by merged PR #6951 and `research/owner-indexed-y0-clearance`. It does not redo the y0 defect (#6951), the declared-family coupling lock (#6945), or the one-edge `C1 Q` row (#6961).

Overlap snapshot on 2026-11-10, via `scripts/find_overlap.py`: local notes at that base (10178 paths, complete inventory), 317 open-PR records fetched at 08:49:48Z, and 6971 discussion records fetched at 08:50:49Z. Requiring both phrases `three-term x1` and `owner-indexed` matches the predecessor package and discussion reply 19507118, which ask this question, and no open PR. Closed PR bodies were outside that snapshot. The search is not a novelty certificate.

## Validation

Python 3.12, standard library only. From the repository root:

```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/owner-indexed-x1-obstruction --check-only
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/owner-indexed-x1-obstruction
```

Both registered commands passed locally, including the optimized run. Checks are explicit `need` failures, not assertions. The run prints `PASS_OWNER_INDEXED_X1_OBSTRUCTION` and `new_kappa None`.

Not run: multipliers with a nonzero D exponent, owner-mixing maps, any feedback operator other than the published pair, quotients by further physical relations, and any tape or minimum field cost.

The one-edge `C1 Q` row is `research/active-feedback-outside-edge`. The gauge engine remains `research/coded-native-caller/gauge.py`.

Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance.

## Open next questions

The package records two follow-ups.

Can one owner-indexed multiplier whose D exponent is not zero cancel `Q^{-1} C1 Q^2 C1 C3 D1 D3` while keeping `x0 = D1 Q^{-1}`, keeping y0 zero, and leaving the four banks stored? The first step is to add one term of D exponent `(0,-1)` to the sharp index above and recompute the four columns. This proof separates the D1 and D1 D3 lines only for a D-exponent-0 factor.

Does one physical relation omitted by this formal algebra send that residual word to zero without collapsing `Q^{-1} C1`? The first step is to name one source relation outside `Q^4 = C1^2 = C3^2 = I` and the inherited D conjugation rule, then reduce only that word. No such relation is imposed here. A quotient that kills the residual would still not be an autonomous caller.

## Workflow feedback (optional)

The x1 column is an identity once the four banks are expanded, so a bounded word search is the wrong instrument. The parity character finishes the infinite family in one step. Link once: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1200
